title: Forgetting Knowledge
chinese: 取天下常以无事，及其有事，不足以取天下。
pinyin: Wèi xué rì yì， wèi dào rì sǔn。
Sǔn zhī yòu sǔn， yǐ zhì yú wú wèi。
Wú wèi ér wú bù wèi。
Qǔ tiān xià cháng yǐ wú shì， jí qí yǒu shì， bù zú yǐ qǔ tiān xià。
english: He who devotes himself to learning (seeks) from day to day to increase (his knowledge); he who devotes himself to the Tao (seeks) from day to day to diminish (his doing).
He diminishes it and again diminishes it, till he arrives at doing nothing (on purpose). Having arrived at this point of non-action, there is nothing which he does not do.
He who gets as his own all under heaven does so by giving himself no trouble (with that end). If one take trouble (with that end), he is not equal to getting as his own all under heaven.
